import json

with open('crash/09793.json') as f:
    test = json.load(f)

ch = test['channels']['vehicle_x']
rate = round(1 / ch['dt'])
print(ch['comment'], ch['code'], ch['unit'])
print('dt =', ch['dt'], 's, so the rate is', rate, 'Hz')

G = 9.81
y = []                           # the crossmember in g
for v in ch['y']:
    y.append(v / G)


def peak(values):
    """The largest size in values, ignoring sign."""
    biggest = abs(values[0])
    for v in values:
        if abs(v) > biggest:
            biggest = abs(v)
    return biggest


full = peak(y)
i_peak = 0                       # the index of the largest size
for i in range(len(y)):
    if abs(y[i]) > abs(y[i_peak]):
        i_peak = i
print(f'peak at the recorded rate: {full:.1f} g, sample {i_peak}, '
      f'{1000 * (ch["t0"] + i_peak * ch["dt"]):.2f} ms')

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

factors = [1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 40, 50, 100, 200, 400]
rates = []
peaks = []
for k in factors:
    rates.append(rate / k)
    peaks.append(peak(y[::k]))    # every k-th sample, from sample 0
    print(f'{rate / k:7.0f} Hz  {peaks[-1]:6.1f} g  {100 * peaks[-1] / full:5.1f}%')

plt.semilogx(rates, peaks, 'o-')
plt.axvline(1000, color='red')
plt.xlabel('sample rate (Hz, log scale)')
plt.ylabel('peak read from the record (g)')
plt.title('Crossmember peak keeping every k-th sample, from sample 0')
plt.show()

k = rate // 1000     # 20, so a 1000 Hz logger keeps one sample in 20
at_1k = []           # the peak for each starting sample s
for s in range(k):
    at_1k.append(peak(y[s::k]))
rounded = []
for p in at_1k:
    rounded.append(round(p, 1))
print(rounded)
print(f'lowest {min(at_1k):.1f} g, highest {max(at_1k):.1f} g, '
      f'average {sum(at_1k) / k:.1f} g')

plt.plot(range(k), at_1k, 'o')
plt.axhline(full, color='gray', linestyle='--')
plt.xticks(range(k))
plt.xlabel('first sample kept (0 to 19)')
plt.ylabel('peak read at 1000 Hz (g)')
plt.title('Crossmember peak at 1000 Hz, for each starting sample')
plt.show()

def peaks_by_start(y, k):
    """Peak of every k-th sample, for each of the k possible starts."""
    peaks = []
    for s in range(k):
        peaks.append(peak(y[s::k]))
    return peaks

check_rates = [10000, 5000, 2000, 1000, 500]
typical = {}
print('typical % of the 20 kHz peak (worst start in brackets)')
for key, c in test['channels'].items():
    yy = c['y']                 # a percentage does not need the units
    top = peak(yy)
    typical[key] = []
    line = f'{key:12}'
    for r in check_rates:
        p = peaks_by_start(yy, rate // r)
        typical[key].append(100 * sum(p) / len(p) / top)
        line = line + f' {typical[key][-1]:5.1f} ({100 * min(p) / top:4.1f})'
    print(line)

for key, c in test['channels'].items():
    plt.semilogx(check_rates, typical[key], 'o-', label=key)
plt.axhline(90, color='black', linestyle=':', label='90%')
plt.axvline(1000, color='red')
plt.xlabel('sample rate (Hz, log scale)')
plt.ylabel('typical peak (% of the 20 kHz peak)')
plt.title('Average over every starting sample, all eight channels')
plt.legend(fontsize=8)
plt.show()
